items.text:
नमः कमलनाभाय नमस्ते जलशायिने।
नमस्ते केशवानन्त वासुदेव नमोऽस्तुते॥
items.tr:
namaḥ kamalanābhāya namaste jalaśāyine|
namaste keśavānanta vāsudeva namo'stute||
items.en: Salutation to the lotus-navelled one; salutation to you who lie on the waters. Salutation to you, Keshava, endless one; salutation to you, Vasudeva.

items.text:
नमो ब्रह्मण्यदेवाय गोब्राह्मणहिताय च।
जगद्धिताय कृष्णाय गोविंदाय नमो नमः॥
items.tr:
namo brahmaṇyadevāya gobrāhmaṇahitāya ca|
jagaddhitāya kṛṣṇāya goviṃdāya namo namaḥ||
items.en: Again and again salutation to Krishna, Govinda, the God devoted to the holy, who does good to cows and Brahmins and to the whole world.

items.text:
आकाशात्पतितं तोयं यथा गच्छति सागरम्।
सर्वदेवनमस्कारः केशवं प्रति गच्छति॥
items.tr:
ākāśātpatitaṃ toyaṃ yathā gacchati sāgaram|
sarvadevanamaskāraḥ keśavaṃ prati gacchati||
items.en: Just as rain falling from the sky goes to the ocean, so a salutation offered to any god goes to Keshava.

items.text:
एष निष्कण्टकः पन्था यत्र संपूज्यते हरिः।
कुपथं तं विजानीयाद् गोविन्दरहितागमम्॥
items.tr:
eṣa niṣkaṇṭakaḥ panthā yatra saṃpūjyate hariḥ|
kupathaṃ taṃ vijānīyād govindarahitāgamam||
items.en: Where Hari is worshipped, that path is free of thorns. Know that any teaching without Govinda is a wrong path.

items.text:
सर्ववेदेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वतीर्थेषु यत्फलम्।
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति स्तुत्वा देवं जनार्दनम्॥
items.tr:
sarvavedeṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu yatphalam|
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti stutvā devaṃ janārdanam||
items.en: Whatever merit there is in all the Vedas, and whatever fruit in all the holy places, a person gains that fruit by praising God Janardana.

items.text:
यो नरः पठते नित्यं त्रिकालं केशवालये।
द्विकालमेककालं वा क्रूरं सर्वं व्यपोहति॥
items.tr:
yo naraḥ paṭhate nityaṃ trikālaṃ keśavālaye|
dvikālamekakālaṃ vā krūraṃ sarvaṃ vyapohati||
items.en: A person who reads this daily in a temple of Keshava, three times, twice or once a day, removes everything harsh.

items.text:
दह्यन्ते रिपवस्तस्य सौम्याः सर्वे सदा ग्रहाः।
विलीयन्ते च पापानि स्तवे ह्यस्मिन् प्रकीर्तिते॥
items.tr:
dahyante ripavastasya saumyāḥ sarve sadā grahāḥ|
vilīyante ca pāpāni stave hyasmin prakīrtite||
items.en: When this hymn is recited, his enemies are burned up, all the planets are always kind to him, and his sins melt away.

items.text:
येन ध्यातः श्रुतो येन येनायं पठ्यते स्तवः।
दत्तानि सर्वदानानि सुराः सर्वे समर्चिताः॥
items.tr:
yena dhyātaḥ śruto yena yenāyaṃ paṭhyate stavaḥ|
dattāni sarvadānāni surāḥ sarve samarcitāḥ||
items.en: One who meditates on this hymn, hears it or reads it has, as it were, given every gift and worshipped all the gods.

items.text:
इह लोके परे वापि न भयं विद्यते क्वचित्।
नाम्नां सहस्रं योऽधीते द्वादश्यां मम सन्निधौ॥
items.tr:
iha loke pare vāpi na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit|
nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ yo'dhīte dvādaśyāṃ mama sannidhau||
items.en: Whoever studies the thousand names on the twelfth day of the moon in my presence has no fear anywhere, in this world or the next.

items.text:
शनैर्दहन्ति पापानि कल्पकोटिशतानि च।
अश्वत्थसन्निधौ पार्थ ध्यात्वा मनसि केशवम्॥
items.tr:
śanairdahanti pāpāni kalpakoṭiśatāni ca|
aśvatthasannidhau pārtha dhyātvā manasi keśavam||
items.en: Arjuna, sins of hundreds of millions of ages are slowly burned away when one sits near a holy fig tree with Keshava in the mind,

items.text:
पठेन्नामसहस्रं तु गवां कोटिफलं लभेत्।
शिवालये पठेनित्यं तुलसीवनसंस्थितः॥
items.tr:
paṭhennāmasahasraṃ tu gavāṃ koṭiphalaṃ labhet|
śivālaye paṭhenityaṃ tulasīvanasaṃsthitaḥ||
items.en: and reads the thousand names; one gains the merit of giving ten million cows. One who reads it daily in a temple of Shiva, sitting in a grove of tulasi,

items.text:
नरो मुक्तिमवाप्नोति चक्रपाणेर्वचो यथा।
ब्रह्महत्यादिकं घोरं सर्वपापं विनश्यति॥
items.tr:
naro muktimavāpnoti cakrapāṇervaco yathā|
brahmahatyādikaṃ ghoraṃ sarvapāpaṃ vinaśyati||
items.en: gains liberation, as the holder of the discus has said. All terrible sins, even the killing of a Brahmin, are destroyed.

items.text:
विलयं यान्ति पापानि चान्यपापस्य का कथा।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति॥
items.tr:
vilayaṃ yānti pāpāni cānyapāpasya kā kathā|
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati||
items.en: Such sins dissolve, so what need is there to speak of other sins? Freed from all sins, he goes to the world of Vishnu.
